# QATQ v0.4.5: Faster lossless tensor compression

QATQ v0.4.5 speeds up exact tensor encoding and decoding and reduces chunked QATC file sizes. QATQ 0.4.4 can still read files produced by the default encoder.

## What changed

- Byte-plane transforms, reusable Zstd contexts, and buffered I/O speed up the codec and chunked CLI.
- Flushing byte planes within a standard Zstd frame improves compression using the existing QATQ format.
- The public Rust strategy enum stays compatible with exhaustive matches. Compression and decompression fall back to fresh Zstd contexts during thread shutdown.

## Measured results

| Apple M4 workload | Compared with QATQ 0.4.4 |
| --- | ---: |
| Chunked QATC encode throughput | 2.85× |
| Chunked QATC decode throughput | 1.31× |
| Total chunked QATC size | 7.28% smaller |
| 4 KiB encode throughput after the compatibility fixes | 2.23× |

The chunked comparison used 14 real llama.cpp KV-cache captures from Phi-4 Mini and Qwen2.5 1.5B across f16, bf16, and f32. It used 65,536 values per chunk and three interleaved release-mode runs per capture and build. The 4 KiB comparison used 12 slices from the same captures, with five interleaved runs of 150 iterations per build. Throughput figures are geometric means of per-fixture median speed ratios. The final fixes preserved the earlier candidate's output bytes on all 26 inputs and passed 78 byte-for-byte cross-version decode checks. See the [performance PR](https://github.com/kabudu/qatq/pull/51) and [changelog](https://github.com/kabudu/qatq/blob/v0.4.5/CHANGELOG.md).
